pairs.why: A keeps the soft, compact canopy of puffy panels with no visible ribs, like the real card, while B shows its rib frame and pole hardware, which is the fussy mechanical build the art lead marks down.
B's fewer, thicker, rounded panels read closer to the real umbrella's chunky lobes than A's thinner scalloped edge, though the two are close.
A has big, chunky, stylized ice cubes and fills the frame the way the real card does, while B is a smaller, more photographic glass with tiny ice.
A's tall tapered glass, larger size and straw running diagonally through the drink match the real card better than B's small, photographic glass.
A's chunky ice and bright orange colour masses match the real card's stylized look, while B leans photoreal, though A is a little too glossy.

B's few thick, rounded branches and simple rock base match the real coral's silhouette, while A's thin, busy branching and grainy texture read as too detailed, though B is somewhat too glossy and saturated.
Both have thin, many-branched coral, but B's calmer colours and mid-green background are closer to the real card than A's brighter lime.
Both have thin, textured branches, but B's calmer palette and background match the real card slightly better than A's brighter, busier version.
